subject: Legacy pool decommission: Stellaris pilot impact & temporary reservation request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Amanda Chen <amanda@stellaris.ai>
Cc: procurement@stellaris.ai
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Legacy pool decommission: Stellaris pilot impact & temporary reservation request

Team —

Heads-up: infra is scheduling the decommission of "legacy-dedicated-pool-3" (the 1U A100 pool customers were routed to during onboarding) for maintenance and capacity consolidation. Target decommission window is 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-03 (final cutover on 09/01 morning). This will evict any live reservations that still reference that pool.

Why this matters: Stellaris AI is running their pilot (deal HUB-7321) in that pool this month and they have a customer-facing demo on 2026-09-08. Product has also scheduled internal canary tests the week after. We need a cross-functional decision on whether to:

- Carve a temporary reservation (preferred), or
- Migrate them to a compatible slate ahead of time, or
- Delay decommission for their demo window (least preferred).

Immediate ask: I propose we create a temporary reservation equivalent to 2x A100-80GB capacity (or our closest equivalent) from 2026-09-01 08:00 PDT through 2026-09-14 23:59 PDT, and apply an autoscale policy exemption so scale-to-zero won't evict the cache during the demo.

Please reply with the following by EOD Tue (24 Aug):
- Infra (Kimberly): feasibility + rough cost delta for a 2-week carveout + whether we can scope a narrow exemption just for the reservation (not blanket).
- Product (Laura): confirm which demo features must be run on the legacy pool (KV cache sensitivity, seq length expectations). If we accept reduced headroom, what’s the minimum throughput for the demo?
- Dev/CS (Dev/Grace): I'll coordinate communications with Stellaris and procurement — confirm timing constraints they provided.

Attachments: I pulled a quick usage snapshot for their pilot (stellaris-usage-snapshot.csv).

Thanks —
Marcus Lin
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Amanda Chen <amanda@stellaris.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Legacy pool decommission: Stellaris pilot impact & temporary reservation request

Marcus —

Thanks for the flag. Short answer: feasible, but I need some telemetry to size it correctly. A few notes:

1) Reservation options: we can (A) carve a short-lived reservation on another dedicated slate (same hw class) or (B) create a soft reservation on our burst lane with higher preemption risk. Option A is preferred for stability, Option B is cheaper but not safe for customer demos.

2) Autoscale exemption: we can scope an exemption tied to a reservation ID so it won't affect other pools. That will require an ops ticket and +1 day lead time.

3) Telemetry I need from you/Dev for sizing: average concurrent requests (p99 qps), typical sequence length, KV cache hit rate, and percent of streaming vs non-streaming calls. If you can't get full numbers, give peak/session and we'll pad by 30%.

I've attached an initial estimate worksheet: decommission-impact-estimate.xlsx (contains the modeling assumptions). Based on the snapshot you attached, a 2x A100-80GB equivalent reservation for 14 days looks reasonable but cost will be ~12% above baseline for that window due to rebalancing.

Action items from infra:
- If we proceed with carveout, submit ops ticket by 2026-08-25 EOD.
- We'll tag the reservation with a canary policy so we can observe degradation without impacting global autoscaling.

I'll standby for the sizing numbers.

—Kimberly
Head of Infra Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Amanda Chen <amanda@stellaris.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Legacy pool decommission: Stellaris pilot impact & temporary reservation request

Quick context from product/roadmap:

- The Stellaris demo on 2026-09-08 is customer-facing and showcases our low-latency KV cache behavior for multi-turn medical summaries. The demo succeeds if p50 latency for typical flows stays < 250ms and there are no cold-cache penalties during the 30-minute demo window.
- We can accept reduced batch headroom outside the demo window, but the demo itself needs the reservation to be dedicated (no preemption).
- We also have an internal canary on 2026-09-10 that exercises longer seq-length sweeps; for that test we can accept brief throttling but prefer not to.

Given the above, product supports the 2x A100-80GB equivalent reservation for 2026-09-01 — 2026-09-14 but we need an SLA override for the 09/08 demo window (08:00–12:00 PDT) so customer-facing traffic gets guarded.

Related: HubSpot shows a DocuSign envelope pending for a supplementary SLA addendum (see link). If procurement signs that by 09/03 we can treat this as a paid reservation and avoid manual credits.

Laura
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Amanda Chen <amanda@stellaris.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Legacy pool decommission: Stellaris pilot impact & temporary reservation request

Thanks all — summary and next steps below.

Decision: carve a temporary reservation. Details: 2x A100-80GB equivalent reservation ID RES-2026-091 (internal), window 2026-09-01 08:00 PDT through 2026-09-14 23:59 PDT. Autoscale exemption scoped to RES-2026-091 to prevent scale-to-zero during the demo window.

Costs & approvals: Kimberly's estimate puts the incremental cost at ~12% for the two-week window. Laura, we will treat the 09/08 demo as SLA-protected hours. Grace/Dev: please confirm final text for customer comms; I'll send the note to Stellaris once we have procurement's sign-off.

Action owners:
- Kimberly: create ops ticket and tag reservation (due 2026-08-25 EOD).
- Dev: provide final telemetry numbers (concurrent qps, seq length distribution) by 2026-08-24 noon — if not available, use the snapshot Marcus attached +30%.
- Grace: coordinate with Amanda/stellaris procurement to push DocuSign by 2026-09-03.
- Marcus: send confirmation to Stellaris and update HubSpot (HUB-7321) once ops ticket exists.

Attachments referenced: decommission-impact-estimate.xlsx, stellaris-usage-snapshot.csv

Marcus
Senior Product Manager, Dedicated
Redwood Inference
